Note: page.fill on <input type=number> in KonfigurasiCuti was flaky when chained across two number fields — use keyboard.type instead in future scripts.
rca of the issue: No blockers. During initial Playwright run, chained page.fill on two adjacent number inputs (konfig-saldo-bersama then konfig-saldo-n) resulted in the first field's value being reverted to 0 before save fired (PUT sent bersama=0). Root cause is a Playwright/React interplay with controlled `<input type=number>`: page.fill dispatches an 'input' event on the DOM element but React's synthetic event system, combined with subsequent focus changes on the second input, occasionally re-runs the render cycle with the original number value before the state commit completes. Reproduced deterministically; fixed by using page.keyboard.type after Ctrl+A/Delete (which mimics real keystrokes and each keystroke triggers a stable React state update). PUT payload then correctly showed default_saldo_bersama=3 and persisted. This is a TEST-SCRIPT limitation, not an application bug — real users typing values work as expected.
